items.stem:
The oxygen moves into a liquid in the body when it leaves the lungs. This liquid takes the oxygen around the body.

Write down the name of this liquid.

Priya says, 'Many vertebrates have similar respiratory systems to humans. These animals have lungs and breathe in oxygen from the air.'

Choose all the animals with similar respiratory systems to humans.
items.note: Both correct for the mark.

items.stem:
Viruses and bacteria infect humans and cause disease.

Write down one other cause of disease which infects humans.
items.note: Mark scheme: parasite or fungus/fungi.

items.stem:
Good hygiene helps to control the spread of diseases. Washing our hands is important for good hygiene.

Complete the sentences.

We must wash our hands because …
We always need to wash our hands when …

accepted: washing removes bacteria or viruses from our hands; we touch food
it removes germs from our hands; we have used the toilet
washing kills bacteria or viruses; after using the toilet
it removes bacteria, viruses, parasites or fungi from our hands; before touching food or after using the toilet

items.note: 1 mark each. Sentence 1: (idea that) washing removes/kills bacteria or viruses or parasites or fungi from our hands (ignore just 'washing controls the spread of disease'; accept other suitable reasons). Sentence 2: (idea of) touching food, using the toilet, looking after someone who is sick, blowing your nose, touching an animal. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
Oliver investigates the temperature change when a solid reacts with a solution. He adds 25 cm³ of the solution to a beaker, adds a small piece of the solid, stirs the mixture all the time and records the temperature for five minutes.

Name the equipment Oliver uses to accurately measure 25 cm³ of the solution.
items.note: Mark scheme: measuring cylinder. Ignore just pipette / measuring scale / litre scale. Do not accept beaker or measuring cup.

items.stem:
Oliver stirs the mixture all the time during the investigation.

Explain why this makes his results more accurate.

accepted: to make sure the temperature is the same throughout the mixture
so the temperature is the same all through the mixture
to make sure all the solid has reacted
so the heat is spread evenly through the mixture

items.note: Mark scheme: (idea of) to make sure the temperature is the same throughout the mixture. Accept: to make sure all the solid has reacted. Ignore: to make sure the solution and solid are completely mixed / to help the solid dissolve. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
Oliver says, 'At the start of the investigation the solid is grey and the solution is blue. At the end of the investigation the solid is brown and the solution is colourless.'

Complete these sentences about the investigation.

The colour of the reactant solution is …
The colour of the solid product is …

Write the two colours in order, separated by a comma.
items.note: Both correct for the mark: reactant solution blue; solid product brown.

items.stem:
Temperature change and colour change are observations that show a chemical reaction happens.

Write down one other observation that shows a chemical reaction happens.
items.note: Mark scheme: gas produced. Accept bubbles (seen).

items.stem:
Look at Oliver's results table.

Complete the sentences to describe the pattern in the results.

From … minutes until 2 minutes the temperature is increasing.
From 2 minutes until … minutes the temperature is … .
There are … anomalous results.

Write the four missing words or numbers in order, separated by commas.
items.note: Mark scheme: 0 or 1; 5; decreasing; 0 or no. All four correct for the mark.

items.stem:
Boiling and evaporation are physical changes.

Choose all the correct statements about boiling and evaporation.
options: boiling only happens from the surface of a liquid
boiling produces bubbles in the liquid

correct: boiling produces bubbles in the liquid

items.note: Each correct answer = 1 mark. Three boxes ticked with two correct = 1 mark; four or five ticked = 0 marks.

items.stem:
Physical changes are reversible.

Match each process to the reverse of the process.
items.note: All three lines correct for the mark. On paper the right-hand column has only two entries (freezing, condensation); condensation is the reverse of both evaporation and boiling.

items.stem:
Thermal conductivity is a property of a material.

What is the meaning of thermal conductivity?

accepted: the rate at which heat is conducted
the rate at which heat is transferred
how good a material is at transferring heat
how well a material conducts heat
how quickly heat passes through a material

items.note: Mark scheme: the rate at which heat is conducted/transferred or how fast heat is conducted/transferred. Accept: the ability to transfer heat / how good a material is at transferring heat. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
Safia collects information about the thermal conductivity of different materials (see her notes).

Use the information to complete the table. The table has two columns: the first column heading is missing and lists air, aluminium, copper, gold, iron and water; the second column is 'thermal conductivity in units'.

Write the missing column heading, then the six values in the order air, aluminium, copper, gold, iron, water, all separated by commas.
items.note: Mark scheme: heading 'material' and all numbers correct for the mark (air 0.024, aluminium 240, copper 380, gold 320, iron 50, water 0.6). Do not accept units written in the body of the table.

items.stem:
Safia says, 'Metals are materials that have a high thermal conductivity.'

Use the information about thermal conductivity to explain why Safia is correct.

accepted: metals have higher numbers than non-metals
the metals have higher thermal conductivity numbers
gold, copper, aluminium and iron all have much higher numbers than water and air

items.note: Mark scheme: (idea that) metals have higher numbers (than non-metals). Accept examples, e.g. copper has the highest number. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
Chen pushes a shopping trolley. The force diagram shows four forces acting on the shopping trolley, drawn as arrows.

Match each arrow to the name of the force. Choose from: applied force, friction, gravity, normal force, upthrust, water resistance.
items.note: All four correct = 2 marks; one, two or three correct = 1 mark. The distractors upthrust and water resistance cannot be shown in the matching format.

items.stem:
Chen walks forward as he pushes the trolley. Force A (pointing backwards) is the same size as force B (pointing forwards).

Describe what happens to the trolley.

accepted: it moves at the same speed
it moves at the same pace
it moves at the same rate
it keeps moving at a steady speed
it moves at a constant speed

items.note: Mark scheme: (idea that) moves with the same pace / at the same rate / does not get faster / does not get slower / the motion stays the same. Accept: moves at the same speed. Do not accept: the trolley does not move. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
A force diagram is a model. A force diagram shows the name and size of the forces.

Describe one other way a force diagram helps Chen to understand forces.

accepted: it shows forces that cannot be seen
it shows the direction of the forces
it shows which way the forces act

items.note: Mark scheme: any one from — forces cannot be seen; shows the direction of forces. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
An astronaut lands on the Moon. He puts a camera onto the surface of the Moon.

What is the weight of the camera on the Moon? Choose the correct answer.

There is less gravity on the Moon than on the Earth.

Choose the two correct sentences.
options: The mass of the camera on Earth is measured in kg.
The mass of the camera on the Moon is measured in m².
The mass of the camera is greater on Earth than on the Moon.
The weight of the camera is greater on Earth than on the Moon.
Gravity makes the camera sink below the surface of the Moon.

correct: The mass of the camera on Earth is measured in kg.
The weight of the camera is greater on Earth than on the Moon.

items.note: Each correct answer = 1 mark. Three boxes ticked with two correct = 1 mark; four or five ticked = 0 marks.

items.stem:
We use symbols to draw electrical circuits. The table shows three circuit symbols.

Write the name of each symbol, in order from top to bottom, separated by commas.

accepted: buzzer, open switch, battery of cells
buzzer, open switch, battery of two cells

items.note: Mark scheme: buzzer; open switch; battery (of cells) or two cells. All three correct for the mark. Do not accept closed switch or just 'switch'.

items.stem:
Jamila investigates soil. She mixes soil with water, adds the mixture to a glass container and waits 10 minutes. The diagram shows the results.

Jamila waits 10 minutes before observing the results. Predict what she observes if she only waits 1 minute before looking at the results.

accepted: the different substances in the soil will be mixed together
there will be no clear layers
the substances have not settled into layers yet
the water will still be cloudy with everything mixed up
only the gravel has started to settle at the bottom

items.note: Mark scheme: (idea that) the different substances in the soil will be mixed together / there will be no clear layers / the substances have not settled into layers yet. Accept references to gravel beginning to settle at the bottom. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
Soils are classified based on the amount of sand, clay and X in the soil. X is labelled on the diagram (the layer floating on top of the water).

What is the name of X?
items.note: Mark scheme: organic content. Accept humus.

items.stem:
Look at the diagram of Jamila's soil results.

Complete the sentence: The volume of sand particles in the soil is … cm³.
items.note: Mark scheme: 24 (cm³).

items.stem:
Some plants do not grow well in this soil. The roots die because the soil traps too much water.

Suggest two different ways to improve this soil to help plants grow well.

1 …
2 …

accepted: reduce the amount of clay; add more gravel
add more gravel; improve the drainage
reduce the amount of clay; add compost
improve the drainage; add organic content

items.note: Each correct answer = 1 mark. Any two from: reduce the amount of clay; add more gravel; improve the drainage; add compost or organic content. Accept any reasonable suggestion to improve the soil. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
The diagram shows part of the Solar System (not drawn to scale).

Name planet A, planet B and planet C. Write the three names in order, separated by commas.
items.note: All three correct for the mark: A Saturn, B Uranus, C Neptune.

items.stem: Name the object that moves around the Earth.
items.note: Mark scheme: Moon. Accept (natural) satellite or a named artificial satellite.

items.stem:
The diagram of the solar system is a model.

Complete the sentences about the diagram of the Solar System.

The meaning of 'Not drawn to scale' is …
Planets in the Solar System are not usually in a straight line because …

accepted: the planets are not the correct size compared to each other; the planets are orbiting the Sun
the planets are not the correct distance from each other; the planets orbit the Sun at different speeds
the sizes and distances are not correct; they are all orbiting the Sun

items.note: 1 mark each. Not drawn to scale: (idea that) the planets are not the correct size (when compared to each other) or not the correct distance (from each other). Not in a straight line: (idea that) the planets are orbiting the Sun. A person should check this answer against the mark scheme.

items.stem:
Physical changes take place in humans during puberty.

Match each change to the correct part of the table: girls only, boys only, or both girls and boys.
items.note: All five correct = 2 marks; two, three or four correct = 1 mark.

omitted.why: Complete the diagram using arrows to show the direction oxygen moves from the air into the left lung — needs arrows drawn on a diagram. [1 mark]
Plot the results for 3, 4 and 5 minutes on the line graph and complete the curve — needs plotting and drawing on a graph. [2 marks]
Draw a parallel circuit with three lamps, one cell and one closed switch using circuit symbols — needs a drawing. [2 marks]
